questions.q: What is the key difference between Change Data Capture and a custom platform event you define yourself?
options: CDC events cannot be subscribed to from Apex
With CDC, Salesforce automatically publishes a change event on create/update/delete/undelete; with a custom event, your own Apex or Flow must call the publish logic
Custom platform events are always high-volume and CDC events are always standard-volume
CDC only works with custom objects, never standard objects
questions.explain: CDC publishes automatically whenever an enabled object's records change through any path, with no publish code of your own. A custom platform event only publishes when your own Apex/Flow explicitly calls EventBus.publish() or the Flow equivalent.

questions.q: If CDC is enabled on the custom object `Invoice__c`, what is the generated change-event channel name?
questions.explain: CDC replaces the __c suffix with __ChangeEvent and publishes under the /data/ channel prefix, so Invoice__c becomes /data/Invoice__ChangeEvent.

questions.q: Which changeType values can appear in a ChangeEventHeader?
options: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, UNDELETE (plus GAP_* variants)
questions.explain: The documented changeType values are CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, UNDELETE, plus GAP_ prefixed variants and GAP_OVERFLOW used for gap-event recovery scenarios.

questions.q: A CDC trigger needs to react only when the BillingCountry field changes on Account, not on every update. Which ChangeEventHeader field should it check?
questions.explain: changedFields lists the fields actually modified by an update, letting the subscriber react only when a specific field it cares about was part of the change.

questions.q: Why might a real design use both CDC and a custom platform event together, rather than only one?
options: CDC can only be enabled on one object per org, so a custom event is needed for everything else
A CDC event on an object can trigger Apex that then publishes a custom event carrying a derived business fact CDC's raw field changes can't express on their own
Custom platform events cannot carry more than one field, so CDC must supply the rest
This combination is never valid in Salesforce
questions.explain: CDC reports raw field-level changes automatically; a custom event can carry a calculated business fact (like 'invoice overdue') that your own Apex derives after reacting to the underlying CDC change.
